evals.prompt: can you help me write a skill for triaging my support inbox every morning
evals.expected_output: The builder opens by offering the Quick and Detailed paths and names which a beginner should take, before starting discovery.
expectations: The first turn offers two paths, a quick one and a detailed one
The response says which path a beginner or unsure user should pick
No SKILL.md is written in this first turn
evals.source: offer two paths in plain language and say which one a

evals.prompt: write me a prompt for summarizing long documents
evals.expected_output: No skill is built; this asks for a prompt, not a skill.
expectations: No SKILL.md is produced
No slash command name is asked for
The response addresses the prompt request directly
evals.source: Use when the user says "build me a skill", "make a skill for..."

evals.prompt: I need a skill that tracks my tasks and pings me when something is overdue
evals.expected_output: The builder backs the user out of solution framing and into the underlying problem before continuing.
expectations: The builder reflects the request back rather than accepting it as the problem
The builder asks what goes wrong today
No skill is drafted from the solution framing as given
evals.source: They've given you a solution, not a problem.

evals.prompt: it's just inefficient, you know? I lose track of stuff sometimes
evals.expected_output: The builder does not move on to behaviour discovery on this answer; it pushes once for a concrete instance.
expectations: The builder asks for a specific example of the last time this happened
The interview does not advance to the behaviour phase
The vague answer is not treated as sufficient
evals.source: Don't move to Phase 3 until you can answer:

evals.prompt: help me build a skill, I'm in a hurry — just pick a name and go
evals.expected_output: The builder still establishes where the skill will live before settling the name, because the name depends on the format.
expectations: The builder asks whether this is for Claude Code or Claude.ai before fixing a name
A slash command name is not settled before the deployment format is known
evals.source: **Ask this after Step 0c (where it lives), not before

evals.prompt: here's what I want it to do — it should read my notes, then tag them, then file them by project, then send a daily digest
evals.expected_output: The builder asks one question at a time rather than interrogating the whole specification at once.
expectations: Only one question is asked in the response
The questions are not delivered as a numbered or bulleted list of prompts to answer
Follow-up questions are held back rather than stacked
evals.source: One question at a time. Listen, probe, move on.

evals.prompt: I want a skill that helps me with my writing. I don't really know what's wrong with it.
evals.expected_output: The builder consults the roles reference for a role whose root cause matches, then asks the question that names the value rather than the task.
expectations: The builder asks what would stop happening if the problem were solved
The builder does not accept "help with my writing" as a specification
The response is aimed at finding the underlying problem rather than the stated task
evals.source: The pain won't name itself, or the skill feels aimed at the stated task rather than the real problem.

evals.prompt: for the skill we're building, write the section on what it does
evals.expected_output: The section is written as directives to Claude rather than as a description of the skill.
expectations: Sections are written as imperatives or directives rather than as descriptions
Any prose that merely describes the skill is rewritten or cut
Content that does not drive behaviour is omitted
evals.source: the skill you write is instructions to Claude, not documentation

evals.prompt: we're done exploring — generate the skill now
evals.expected_output: The generated SKILL.md includes an anti-patterns section with at least three items.
expectations: The generated SKILL.md contains an anti-patterns or equivalent section
That section holds at least three distinct items
The anti-patterns name actual failure modes rather than restating the positive behaviour
evals.source: Anti-patterns section is mandatory — at least 3 items

evals.prompt: the skill is written and the eval suite passes validation — we're done, right?
evals.expected_output: The builder does not treat validation as completion; it runs the suite against a baseline and produces a benchmark before calling the work done.
expectations: Validation is not presented as the end of the process
The builder states that a benchmark is required before the skill is considered measured
If the loop genuinely cannot run, the builder says so explicitly and hands over the command rather than going quiet
evals.source: You are not finished until `benchmark.json` exists.

evals.prompt: how do I know the eval suite is actually covering the skill?
evals.expected_output: The builder presents the coverage table and names any category that came back empty rather than reporting only a total.
expectations: Coverage is reported per category, not as a single count
A category with no cases is called out as a finding
The count is checked against the 8-12 core range and a departure is explained
evals.source: An empty `gate` or `fence` row is a real finding

evals.prompt: just do the single-file version for now
evals.expected_output: The skill is generated at the conventional Claude Code path with valid frontmatter.
expectations: The skill is written under the skills directory in its own named folder
The file is named SKILL.md
The frontmatter carries at least a name and a description
